question.:question/problem: Find the general solution to the differential equation (in implicit form) $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}=\frac{2 \sqrt{x - 3}}{\sqrt{y - 6}}.$
question.:question/worked-solution:
To find the general solution, we first separate the variables:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{2 \sqrt{x - 3}}{\sqrt{y - 6}} \\ (\sqrt{y - 6})\,\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =2 \sqrt{x - 3}\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we integrate both sides with respect to $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\int (\sqrt{y - 6})\,\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x & =\int (2 \sqrt{x - 3})\,\text{d}x \\ \int (\sqrt{y - 6})\,\frac{\text{d}y}{\cancel{\text{d}x}}\,\cancel{\text{d}x} & =\int (2 \sqrt{x - 3})\,\text{d}x \\ \int (\sqrt{y - 6})\,\text{d}y & =\int (2 \sqrt{x - 3})\,\text{d}x \\ \frac{2 \left(y - 6\right)^{\frac{3}{2}}}{3} & =\frac{4 \left(x - 3\right)^{\frac{3}{2}}}{3}+K \\ \left(y - 6\right)^{\frac{3}{2}} & =2 \left(x - 3\right)^{\frac{3}{2}}+C\end{aligned}
$$

where $C=\frac{3}{2}K.$

Therefore, the general solution to the differential equation (in implicit form) is

$$
\left(y - 6\right)^{\frac{3}{2}}=2 \left(x - 3\right)^{\frac{3}{2}}+C.
$$

question.:question/problem: Find the general solution to the differential equation (in implicit form) $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}=\left(4 x + 20\right) e^{2 - y}.$
question.:question/worked-solution:
To find the general solution, we first separate the variables:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\left(4 x + 20\right) e^{2 - y} \\ (e^{y - 2})\,\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =4 x + 20\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we integrate both sides with respect to $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\int (e^{y - 2})\,\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x & =\int (4 x + 20)\,\text{d}x \\ \int (e^{y - 2})\,\frac{\text{d}y}{\cancel{\text{d}x}}\,\cancel{\text{d}x} & =\int (4 x + 20)\,\text{d}x \\ \int (e^{y - 2})\,\text{d}y & =\int (4 x + 20)\,\text{d}x \\ e^{y - 2} & =2 \left(x + 5\right)^{2}+C\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the general solution to the differential equation (in implicit form) is

$$
e^{y - 2}=2 \left(x + 5\right)^{2}+C.
$$

question.:question/problem: Find the general solution to the differential equation (in implicit form) $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}=\sqrt{1 - \left(y - 3\right)^{2}}$ for $\,|\left(y-3\right)|<1.$
question.:question/worked-solution:
To find the general solution, we first separate the variables:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\sqrt{1 - \left(y - 3\right)^{2}} \\ (\frac{1}{\sqrt{1 - \left(y - 3\right)^{2}}})\,\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =1\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we integrate both sides with respect to $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\int (\frac{1}{\sqrt{1 - \left(y - 3\right)^{2}}})\,\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x & =\int (1)\,\text{d}x \\ \int (\frac{1}{\sqrt{1 - \left(y - 3\right)^{2}}})\,\frac{\text{d}y}{\cancel{\text{d}x}}\,\cancel{\text{d}x} & =\int (1)\,\text{d}x \\ \int (\frac{1}{\sqrt{1 - \left(y - 3\right)^{2}}})\,\text{d}y & =\int (1)\,\text{d}x \\ \arcsin{\left(y - 3 \right)} & =x+C\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the general solution to the differential equation (in implicit form) is

$$
\arcsin{\left(y - 3 \right)}=x+C.
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =2 \cos^{2}{\left(y - 1 \right)} \\ (\sec^{2}{\left(y - 1 \right)})\,\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =2\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we integrate both sides with respect to $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\int (\sec^{2}{\left(y - 1 \right)})\,\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x & =\int (2)\,\text{d}x \\ \int (\sec^{2}{\left(y - 1 \right)})\,\frac{\text{d}y}{\cancel{\text{d}x}}\,\cancel{\text{d}x} & =\int (2)\,\text{d}x \\ \int (\sec^{2}{\left(y - 1 \right)})\,\text{d}y & =\int (2)\,\text{d}x \\ \tan{\left(y - 1 \right)} & =2 x+C\end{aligned}

$$
\tan{\left(y - 1 \right)}=2 x+C.

To find the general solution, we first separate the variables:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\left(12 - 4 x\right) e^{- y - 4} \\ (e^{y + 4})\,\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =12 - 4 x\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we integrate both sides with respect to $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\int (e^{y + 4})\,\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x & =\int (12 - 4 x)\,\text{d}x \\ \int (e^{y + 4})\,\frac{\text{d}y}{\cancel{\text{d}x}}\,\cancel{\text{d}x} & =\int (12 - 4 x)\,\text{d}x \\ \int (e^{y + 4})\,\text{d}y & =\int (12 - 4 x)\,\text{d}x \\ e^{y + 4} & =- 2 \left(x - 3\right)^{2}+C\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the general solution to the differential equation (in implicit form) is

$$
e^{y + 4}=- 2 \left(x - 3\right)^{2}+C.
